name: Kubernetes Platform Health
description: Platform availability, server capacity, storage, etcd, and collection health.

display.name: How to check platform health
display.description: Availability, capacity, and collection coverage answer different questions. Check all three before drawing a conclusion.

spec.text: **Check availability, capacity and collection together.** The gauges identify the busiest measured server or disk. CPU and memory refer to the node operating system. Requests/limits do not represent actual use. Empty data can mean an inapplicable source or a collection gap; see the question-mark descriptions. Device totals exclude loop devices and duplicate bind mounts.

display.name: Ready nodes · %
display.description:
Share of known nodes with the Ready condition. This does not prove that every metrics collector is working.

When to investigate / alert coverage: Node Readiness (native)

display.name: OS collection coverage · %
display.description:
Healthy OS collectors divided by known nodes. Below 100% means at least one server is missing visibility.

When to investigate / alert coverage: missing node OS telemetry · 5m. Checks missing node OS telemetry · 5m. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

display.name: Pods needing attention
display.description:
Counts each Pod once when Pending, Failed, Unknown, or Running but not ready. Completed Jobs are excluded. The list beside this card identifies each Pod. A newly starting Pod may appear briefly; this is a triage list, not an incident declaration.

When to investigate / alert coverage: Pod Ready State / Pods in Waiting State / Pod Completed State (native)

spec.query: count(max by (cluster_name,namespace,pod_name) (label_replace((max by (cluster_name,namespace,pod_name,pod_phase) (last_over_time(kubernetes_state_pod_status_phase{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}",pod_phase!~"Running|Succeeded"}[5m] @ end()) == 1)), "reason", "$1", "pod_phase", "(.*)") or label_replace(((max by (cluster_name,namespace,pod_name) (last_over_time(kubernetes_state_pod_ready{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}",condition="false",pod_phase="Running"}[5m] @ end())) == 1)), "reason", "Running but not ready", "", ""))) or (0 * count(kubernetes_state_pod_status_phase{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}"}))

display.name: Pods to investigate · current state
display.description:
Read the table below the line: cluster, namespace, Pod and observed state. Pending may mean scheduling or image preparation; Failed needs Job/container logs; Running but not ready may mean a failed readiness check. Data can lag by a scrape; completed Jobs are excluded.

When to investigate / alert coverage: Pod Ready State / Pods in Waiting State / Pod Completed State (native)

This is a compact status list, not a trend. Read the names below; expand + more if needed. Open the linked query and select Table view for separate columns. The link carries cluster/namespace filters but opens the current Metrics Explorer period; reselect a historical period when investigating the past.

spec.query: label_join((label_replace((max by (cluster_name,namespace,pod_name,pod_phase) (last_over_time(kubernetes_state_pod_status_phase{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}",pod_phase!~"Running|Succeeded"}[5m] @ end()) == 1)), "reason", "$1", "pod_phase", "(.*)") or label_replace(((max by (cluster_name,namespace,pod_name) (last_over_time(kubernetes_state_pod_ready{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}",condition="false",pod_phase="Running"}[5m] @ end())) == 1)), "reason", "Running but not ready", "", "")), "sre_series", " · ", "cluster_name", "namespace", "pod_name", "reason") or on() label_replace(((0 * count(kubernetes_state_pod_status_phase{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}"}))), "sre_series", "No pods need attention in this scope", "", "")

display.name: Affected pods · restarts in the last hour
display.description:
Sums container restarts within each Pod during a moving hour. The table identifies Pod and namespace. A restart does not prove OOM: inspect Last State, previous logs, readiness/liveness probes and events. Counter resets and scrape intervals affect the estimate.

When to investigate / alert coverage: Restarts for containers (native)

spec.query: label_join(((sum by (cluster_name,namespace,pod_name) (max by (cluster_name,namespace,pod_name,container) (increase(kubernetes_state_container_restarts{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}"}[1h])))) > 0), "sre_series", " · ", "cluster_name", "namespace", "pod_name") or on() label_replace((0 * count(kubernetes_state_container_restarts{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}"})), "sre_series", "No restarts observed in the last hour", "", "")

display.name: Affected workloads · missing copies
display.description:
Only workloads with fewer available copies than configured are listed. The value is the number missing, not a count of failures. Deployment, StatefulSet and DaemonSet names identify the owner. A brief rollout can create a temporary gap. No matching source data stays empty.

When to investigate / alert coverage: Deployment / Daemonset / Statefulset desired replicas (native)

display.name: Operational disks · space used · %
display.description:
Used space divided by used plus space available to applications. Reserved blocks are excluded from this denominator. Each mount is identified. Loop devices are excluded: OS images such as Harvester active.img do not represent growing application data. Each device appears once per server; bind mounts of the same filesystem are not counted as separate disks. Use findmnt -S DEVICE on the server to locate its mounts. Operational view: excludes boot, OEM, runtime mounts and kubelet volume mounts. The Harvester persistent partition and all Harvester data disks remain included. Duplicate bind mounts count once per device. Raw collection and space monitors still cover other writable filesystems.

When to investigate / alert coverage: filesystem below 10 percent available · 15m. Checks filesystem below 10 percent available · 15m. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((((max by (cluster_name,node,device,fstype) (node_filesystem_size_bytes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",job="sre-node",device!~"/dev/loop[0-9]+",fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay|squashfs",mountpoint!~"/var/lib/kubelet/.*|/var/lib/rancher/(rke2|k3s)/agent/kubelet/.*|/boot(/.*)?|/run(/.*)?|/oem"})) - (max by (cluster_name,node,device,fstype) (node_filesystem_free_bytes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",job="sre-node",device!~"/dev/loop[0-9]+",fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay|squashfs",mountpoint!~"/var/lib/kubelet/.*|/var/lib/rancher/(rke2|k3s)/agent/kubelet/.*|/boot(/.*)?|/run(/.*)?|/oem"}))) / clamp_min(((max by (cluster_name,node,device,fstype) (node_filesystem_size_bytes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",job="sre-node",device!~"/dev/loop[0-9]+",fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay|squashfs",mountpoint!~"/var/lib/kubelet/.*|/var/lib/rancher/(rke2|k3s)/agent/kubelet/.*|/boot(/.*)?|/run(/.*)?|/oem"})) - (max by (cluster_name,node,device,fstype) (node_filesystem_free_bytes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",job="sre-node",device!~"/dev/loop[0-9]+",fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay|squashfs",mountpoint!~"/var/lib/kubelet/.*|/var/lib/rancher/(rke2|k3s)/agent/kubelet/.*|/boot(/.*)?|/run(/.*)?|/oem"}))) + (max by (cluster_name,node,device,fstype) (node_filesystem_avail_bytes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",job="sre-node",device!~"/dev/loop[0-9]+",fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay|squashfs",mountpoint!~"/var/lib/kubelet/.*|/var/lib/rancher/(rke2|k3s)/agent/kubelet/.*|/boot(/.*)?|/run(/.*)?|/oem"})), 1)), "sre_series", " · ", "cluster_name", "node", "device"))

display.name: Space used on each host filesystem
display.description:
Filesystem capacity minus free space. Includes the Harvester data disk and distinguishes partitions. Do not add repeated mounts of one device. Loop devices are excluded: OS images such as Harvester active.img do not represent growing application data. Each device appears once per server; bind mounts of the same filesystem are not counted as separate disks. Use findmnt -S DEVICE on the server to locate its mounts. Operational view: excludes boot, OEM, runtime mounts and kubelet volume mounts. The Harvester persistent partition and all Harvester data disks remain included. Duplicate bind mounts count once per device. Raw collection and space monitors still cover other writable filesystems.

When to investigate / alert coverage: filesystem below 10 percent available · 15m. Checks filesystem below 10 percent available · 15m. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

display.name: Capacity of each host filesystem
display.description:
Formatted size of the identified mount. It can differ from raw device capacity or the size requested by a PVC. Loop devices are excluded: OS images such as Harvester active.img do not represent growing application data. Each device appears once per server; bind mounts of the same filesystem are not counted as separate disks. Use findmnt -S DEVICE on the server to locate its mounts. Operational view: excludes boot, OEM, runtime mounts and kubelet volume mounts. The Harvester persistent partition and all Harvester data disks remain included. Duplicate bind mounts count once per device. Raw collection and space monitors still cover other writable filesystems.

When to investigate / alert coverage: filesystem below 10 percent available · 15m. Checks filesystem below 10 percent available · 15m. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

display.name: File entries already used · % of inodes
display.description:
Inodes represent files. They can run out even when bytes remain free. This percentage is calculated only when the inode total is positive. Loop devices are excluded: OS images such as Harvester active.img do not represent growing application data. Each device appears once per server; bind mounts of the same filesystem are not counted as separate disks. Use findmnt -S DEVICE on the server to locate its mounts. Operational view: excludes boot, OEM, runtime mounts and kubelet volume mounts. The Harvester persistent partition and all Harvester data disks remain included. Duplicate bind mounts count once per device. Raw collection and space monitors still cover other writable filesystems.

When to investigate / alert coverage: filesystem below 10 percent free inodes · 15m. Checks filesystem below 10 percent free inodes · 15m. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

display.name: Measured PVC filesystems · space used in %
display.description:
Only PVCs with positive inode statistics are included. Block and unmounted volumes are not treated as full.

When to investigate / alert coverage: PVC filesystem below 10 percent available · 15m. Checks PVC filesystem below 10 percent available · 15m. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline. Capacity forecasts also warn when free space is projected to run out within 12 or 96 hours. This is a trend estimate; inspect growth and available history before acting.

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join(((max by (cluster_name,namespace,persistentvolumeclaim) (kubernetes_kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}"}) and on (cluster_name,namespace,persistentvolumeclaim) (max by (cluster_name,namespace,persistentvolumeclaim) (kubernetes_kubelet_volume_stats_inodes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}"}) > 0)) / (max by (cluster_name,namespace,persistentvolumeclaim) (kubernetes_kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}"}) and on (cluster_name,namespace,persistentvolumeclaim) (max by (cluster_name,namespace,persistentvolumeclaim) (kubernetes_kubelet_volume_stats_inodes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}"}) > 0))), "sre_series", " · ", "cluster_name", "namespace", "persistentvolumeclaim"))

display.name: Space used in measured PVC filesystems
display.description:
Usage reported by the kubelet and storage driver. This is not Longhorn replica storage or the filesystem inside a VM backed by a Block PVC.

When to investigate / alert coverage: PVC filesystem below 10 percent available · 15m. Checks PVC filesystem below 10 percent available · 15m. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline. Capacity forecasts also warn when free space is projected to run out within 12 or 96 hours. This is a trend estimate; inspect growth and available history before acting.

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((max by (cluster_name,namespace,persistentvolumeclaim) (kubernetes_kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}"}) and on (cluster_name,namespace,persistentvolumeclaim) (max by (cluster_name,namespace,persistentvolumeclaim) (kubernetes_kubelet_volume_stats_inodes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}"}) > 0)), "sre_series", " · ", "cluster_name", "namespace", "persistentvolumeclaim"))

display.name: Capacity of measured PVC filesystems
display.description:
Formatted capacity reported by the kubelet. Filesystem metadata can make it smaller than the requested PVC size.

When to investigate / alert coverage: PVC filesystem below 10 percent available · 15m. Checks PVC filesystem below 10 percent available · 15m. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((max by (cluster_name,namespace,persistentvolumeclaim) (kubernetes_kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}"}) and on (cluster_name,namespace,persistentvolumeclaim) (max by (cluster_name,namespace,persistentvolumeclaim) (kubernetes_kubelet_volume_stats_inodes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}"}) > 0)), "sre_series", " · ", "cluster_name", "namespace", "persistentvolumeclaim"))

display.name: PVCs without filesystem usage measurements
display.description:
Collection inventory, including Block volumes and volumes without mounted-filesystem statistics. Missing data is not a usage percentage.

When to investigate / alert coverage: Collection applicability: block and unmounted PVCs have no filesystem percentage

This is a compact status list, not a trend. Read the names below; expand + more if needed. Open the linked query and select Table view for separate columns. The link carries cluster/namespace filters but opens the current Metrics Explorer period; reselect a historical period when investigating the past.

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((label_join((max by (cluster_name,namespace,persistentvolumeclaim) (kubernetes_state_persistentvolumeclaim_request_storage{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}"})) unless on (cluster_name,namespace,persistentvolumeclaim) (max by (cluster_name,namespace,persistentvolumeclaim) (kubernetes_kubelet_volume_stats_inodes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}"}) > 0), "item", " · ", "cluster_name", "namespace", "persistentvolumeclaim")), "sre_series", "", "item"))

display.name: Cluster storage volumes · PV status
display.description:
Bound means attached to a claim; Available means available for a claim; Released requires checking retention policy and data ownership. Released is not always a failure.

When to investigate / alert coverage: Orphaned Persistent Volumes (native)

display.name: Storage requests · PVC status
display.description:
Namespace, claim name, phase, and storage class. Investigate claims that remain Pending.

When to investigate / alert coverage: Orphaned Persistent Volumes (native)

display.name: etcd can see a leader · 1 yes / 0 no
display.description:
Every member should recognize a leader. Zero needs investigation; no data means a valid sample is unavailable.

When to investigate / alert coverage: etcd without leader · 1m. Checks etcd without leader · 1m. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

display.name: Leader changes seen by each etcd member · last hour
display.description:
Do not add the same election observed by multiple members. Repeated elections can indicate instability; restarts also affect the history.

When to investigate / alert coverage: etcd leader changes above 3 in 15m. Checks etcd leader changes above 3 in 15m. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

display.name: etcd operations waiting for agreement
display.description:
Proposals waiting for consensus. A growing queue can indicate slow disks, network problems, or difficulty reaching a majority of members.

When to investigate / alert coverage: etcd pending proposals above 100. Checks etcd pending proposals above 100. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

display.name: etcd operations agreed but not yet applied
display.description:
Committed proposals minus applied proposals, per member. Sustained growth means the stored state is falling behind agreed changes.

When to investigate / alert coverage: etcd apply backlog above 1000. Checks etcd apply backlog above 1000. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

display.name: Failed etcd operations · last 15 minutes
display.description:
Proposals that did not complete through consensus. Compare with elections, connectivity, and logs.

When to investigate / alert coverage: etcd failed proposals in 15m. Checks etcd failed proposals in 15m. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

display.name: etcd write-ahead log write time · p99 in ms
display.description:
99% of write-ahead log flushes completed within this time. Above 10 ms for five minutes is an initial investigation threshold.

When to investigate / alert coverage: etcd WAL p99 above 10ms. Checks etcd WAL p99 above 10ms. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

display.name: etcd database write time · p99 in ms
display.description:
99% of database commits completed within this time. Above 25 ms for five minutes is an initial investigation threshold.

When to investigate / alert coverage: etcd commit p99 above 25ms. Checks etcd commit p99 above 25ms. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

display.name: etcd database quota already used · %
display.description:
Physical database size divided by its quota. Near 100% risks blocking new writes. The initial monitor warns above 80% for ten minutes.

When to investigate / alert coverage: etcd database above 80 percent quota. Checks etcd database above 80 percent quota. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

display.name: etcd metrics collection · 1 working / 0 failed
display.description:
Shows whether each metrics endpoint answered the collector. This does not prove healthy consensus. Also check leadership and expected member count.

When to investigate / alert coverage: etcd scrape failing · 3m. Checks etcd scrape failing · 3m. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline. etcd telemetry disappeared · 5m. Checks etcd telemetry disappeared · 5m. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

display.name: Network round trip between etcd members · p99 in ms
display.description:
Time to contact another member and receive a response. A single-member cluster has no peers, so this chart does not apply. Too few observations can also leave it empty.

When to investigate / alert coverage: Diagnostic context: compare with peer network baseline and leader/commit failures

display.name: CPU busy on each server · %
display.description:
Average utilization across logical processors. Compare sustained high values with CPU limits and slow applications.

When to investigate / alert coverage: Capacity context: high CPU alone is not an outage; correlate service latency and VM scheduler wait

display.name: Memory still available on each server · %
display.description:
Linux MemAvailable divided by MemTotal. Lower values mean less headroom. Kubernetes requests are not used in this calculation.

When to investigate / alert coverage: host OS below 10 percent available RAM · 15m. Checks host OS below 10 percent available RAM · 15m. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

display.name: Disk operations in progress · average
display.description:
Average outstanding I/O at the Linux block layer, including queued and in-service operations. A sustained rise with disk latency suggests contention. On a Kubernetes VM this is its guest block device; on Harvester this is the host device. Do not sum partitions and their parent disks.

When to investigate / alert coverage: host disk response above 20ms · 10m. Average disk response exceeds 20 ms throughout observed samples in a 10-minute window, while the five-minute average activity is at least 1 operation/s. This is an initial investigation threshold, not a universal storage SLA.

display.name: OS pages fetched from disk · pages/s
display.description:
Major page faults require disk I/O; file-backed pages also count. Compare this with available RAM and VM swap charts before concluding memory shortage. Linux PSI panels are omitted because these kernels do not expose PSI.

When to investigate / alert coverage: host OS below 10 percent available RAM · 15m. Checks host OS below 10 percent available RAM · 15m. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

display.name: Server CPU busy · highest · %
display.description:
Shows the highest value among the selected resources at the end of the time window. The resource is named below. Orange starts at 80%, red at 90%; these are initial reference colors, not proof of an outage. See the historical charts for duration and trend. Five-minute CPU utilization averaged across the server logical processors. Namespace does not filter servers.

When to investigate / alert coverage: Capacity context: high CPU alone is not an outage; correlate service latency and VM scheduler wait

display.name: Server memory used · highest · %
display.description:
Shows the highest value among the selected resources at the end of the time window. The resource is named below. Orange starts at 80%, red at 90%; these are initial reference colors, not proof of an outage. See the historical charts for duration and trend. Linux total minus available memory, divided by total. Reclaimable cache is accounted for in available memory. Namespace does not filter servers.

When to investigate / alert coverage: host OS below 10 percent available RAM · 15m. Checks host OS below 10 percent available RAM · 15m. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((last_over_time((topk(1, (1 - (max by (cluster_name,node) (last_over_time(node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",job="sre-node"}[5m])) / max by (cluster_name,node) (last_over_time(node_memory_MemTotal_bytes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",job="sre-node"}[5m]))))))[1s:1s] @ end())), "sre_series", " · ", "cluster_name", "node"))

display.name: Host filesystem used · highest · %
display.description:
Shows the highest value among the selected resources at the end of the time window. The resource is named below. Orange starts at 80%, red at 90%; these are initial reference colors, not proof of an outage. See the historical charts for duration and trend. Used space divided by used plus space available to applications, matching df. The mount and device identify the filesystem. Namespace does not filter host disks. Loop devices are excluded: OS images such as Harvester active.img do not represent growing application data. Each device appears once per server; bind mounts of the same filesystem are not counted as separate disks. Use findmnt -S DEVICE on the server to locate its mounts. Operational view: excludes boot, OEM, runtime mounts and kubelet volume mounts. The Harvester persistent partition and all Harvester data disks remain included. Duplicate bind mounts count once per device. Raw collection and space monitors still cover other writable filesystems.
